readings: The boy Jesus in the Temple
2026-12-29.alt: Mapped from the weekday after the Sunday of Nativity in the 2024–25 calendar; please verify.
2026-12-29.verse: He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
theo: At twelve Jesus stays behind in the Temple; Mary and Joseph search for him for three days in anguish. When they find him, he answers: “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” Even as a boy he knows who his Father is. Then he goes down with them to Nazareth and is obedient to them, growing in wisdom and favour.

Paul gives the rule of Christian family and community life: “Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ… let us not grow weary in doing what is right… let us work for the good of all.” The home at Nazareth was such a place: love that carried, patience that waited, and obedience that grew.
outline: Ask: have you ever lost someone and searched in anguish?
Jesus' first recorded words reveal his identity.
The Son of God obeys his parents.
“I must be in my Father's house.”
live: Take on one burden for a family member this week.
Make a visit to church this week.
2026-12-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were found in your Father's house and lived obediently at Nazareth. Help us bear one another's burdens and grow in wisdom and grace. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we bring the burdens of others to the altar in the prayers of the faithful. Christ, who carried our burden on the Cross, carries them with us.

quick: Jesus knew his Father's house from boyhood.
The Son of God obeyed Mary and Joseph.
2026-12-29.action: Carry one burden for a family member this week.
2026-12-29.question: Where do I search for Jesus when I lose him?

family.explain: Jesus stayed in the Temple, his Father's house. Mary and Joseph were worried, but Jesus went home with them and obeyed them.
family.intention: We pray for parents who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we help carry someone's burden this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were found in your Father's house. As we gather, teach us to bear one another's burdens and to treasure your word like Mary. Amen.
share: Paul says: bear one another's burdens (Galatians 6:2). Whose burden can I help carry?
Mary and Joseph searched in anxiety (Luke 2:48). What anxiety do I bring to God?
How do I correct others: with gentleness or with harshness?
pm.resp: Lord, help us carry one another.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a family where burdens are shared.
For parents searching for lost children, in faith or in life.
For young people, that they may grow in wisdom and grace like Jesus.
For those weary in doing good, that they may not give up.
For our prayer group, that we may support one another faithfully.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son grew in wisdom in the home of Nazareth. Help us bear one another's burdens, never grow weary in doing good, and treasure your word in our hearts. Amen.

illus: A mother in Alappuzha whose son had stopped speaking to the family joined a small group of parents who prayed together every Thursday for their children. “Alone I would have collapsed,” she said. “Together we carried each other.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Galatians: bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ (Galatians 6:2). Christian life is not lived alone. Each of us carries something heavy, and each of us is called to help carry another's load.

Paul is practical: if anyone is detected in a transgression, you who have received the Spirit should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness. Take care that you yourselves are not tempted (Galatians 6:1). Correction must be gentle and humble.

He adds: let us not grow weary in doing what is right, for we will reap at harvest time, if we do not give up. So then, whenever we have an opportunity, let us work for the good of all, and especially for those of the family of faith (Galatians 6:9–10).

In the Gospel the twelve-year-old Jesus stays behind in the Temple. Mary and Joseph search for three days, anxious. When they find him, Mary says: your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety. Jesus answers: did you not know that I must be in my Father's house? (Luke 2:48–49).

Even the Holy Family knew anxiety and misunderstanding. Mary did not fully understand, but she treasured all these things in her heart. Then Jesus went down with them to Nazareth and was obedient to them, and increased in wisdom and in years (Luke 2:51–52).

Many parents today search anxiously for children who are lost: in faith, in addiction, in wrong company, far away abroad. Let us bear one another's burdens: pray for these families, support them, and never grow weary. And let us ask Mary to teach us to treasure and ponder, even when we do not understand. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph at home. Help your parents today without complaining!

intro: The finding in the Temple and the law of mutual burden-bearing.

sub: Samuel grew in favour with God and people.
Jesus grew in wisdom and years.
q: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favor with the LORD and with the people.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Pray for the growth of the children in your family.

sub: Mary and Joseph search in anguish and find him.
q: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rely on your own insight.
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”

sub: The Son of God obeys at Nazareth.
q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them.
points.apply: Carry one burden for a family member.

concl: Jesus belongs to the Father and lives in a family.
Let us seek him and carry one another.
